title: A Tiny Book on Linear Models
subtitle: Least squares and regularization in two chapters

source.citation: *A Tiny Book on Linear Models* — example source written for study-kit (`examples/source/tiny-linear-models/`).

chapters.title: Least Squares
chapters.scope: The linear model in matrix form, the squared loss, the normal equations, the geometry of the fit, stable solvers.
chapters.goal: Fit a linear model by least squares and understand the fit as an orthogonal projection.
chapters.prerequisites: Matrix products, transposes and inverses; derivatives of functions of several variables (stated in the preface).

forward_links.note: ridge modifies the normal equations of §1.3; the invertibility condition is what fails in §2.1

chapters.title: Regularization
chapters.scope: When least squares is unreliable, ridge, lasso, choosing λ by cross-validation.
chapters.goal: Stabilize a linear fit with a penalty and choose its strength without leaking validation data.
chapters.prerequisites: ch01, in particular the normal equations (§1.3).

variants.title: Ordinary least squares only
variants.source: Preface, "How to read this book": readers interested only in ordinary least squares may stop after Chapter 1.
